test.title: login API returns a token
test.error:
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: 200
Received: 423

triage.reason: The API answered with HTTP 423 (Locked), which is the lockout state of the shared demo account `customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com` on the public practicesoftwaretesting service — an external account/service condition, not wrong app logic and not a stale locator. A genuine credential mismatch would return 401, and a broken endpoint would return 4xx/5xx of a different kind. The reproducibility across 3 attempts rules out flakiness. Secondary possibility: the hardcoded password `pass123` is wrong and repeated runs drove the account into lockout, which would make it a broken script; that is why confidence is medium rather than high.
triage.evidence: "Expected: 200 / Received: 423" at `expect(response.status()).toBe(200);` for `request.post('https://api.practicesoftwaretesting.com/users/login', { data: { email: 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com', password: 'pass123' } })` — 423 = Locked.
triage.next_step: Call the login endpoint manually (e.g. curl/Postman) with the documented demo credentials for customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com and inspect the 423 response body/message; if it confirms a lockout, wait out or reset the account (or switch to a dedicated non-shared test user) and verify the password in the test matches the documented one.

The route glob `'**/products'` does not match the app's actual request URL, which carries query parameters (price range, sort, page — all visible in the UI). The test's own setup is wrong, not the app. Failing identically on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness, and the app cannot be blamed for not showing an empty state while it has 9 products.
triage.evidence: Test setup: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` — yet the page under test shows live data: `link "ECO Combination Pliers CO₂: A B C D E $14.15"` and `navigation "Pagination"` with `page 2`, `page 3`. Error: `expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed ... getByText('There are no products found.') ... element(s) not found`.
triage.next_step: Run the test with `DEBUG=pw:api` (or add `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.url()))`) to capture the exact products request URL, then widen the pattern to match it — e.g. `await page.route(/\/products(\?.*)?$/, ...)` or `'**/products?**'` — and confirm the empty-state copy in the Angular template matches the expected string before re-asserting.

triage.reason: The add-to-cart action itself clearly succeeded: the failure-time accessibility tree still shows the Combination Pliers product page with the nav cart badge at "1". So the item went into the cart, but the expected success confirmation ("Product added to shopping cart.") never rendered at any point during the 5 s polling window, and no alternative toast/alert text appears anywhere in the tree. The test's check is reasonable (a confirmation after adding to cart) and it failed identically on all 3 attempts, which rules out timing/flakiness. The page is also running in "Bug Hunting Mode" and already shows other deliberately broken/mutated UI text ("Contakt", "Reltded products", the "Home" link pointing at #/contact), which fits a seeded defect in the confirmation message rather than a stale test. A reworded (not missing) toast would also be an app-side text defect; the only other explanation — the message text legitimately changed in the app and the test is out of date — is less likely given no message of any kind is present.
triage.evidence: Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed — Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.') ... element(s) not found; yet the same snapshot shows `menuitem "cart": - link "cart": - /url: "#/checkout" - text:  1`, i.e. the product was added while no confirmation was shown.
triage.next_step: Manually open a product page in the Toolshop app (chromium), click "Add to cart", and watch the toast area: confirm whether no confirmation appears at all or whether its wording/markup changed — then file the missing/incorrect confirmation message as a bug (and update the locator only if the app's intended text has officially changed).
